assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns a small molecule into a bifunctional or glue-like recognition element that recruits an E3 ligase and removes a protein, rather than merely inhibiting it. This is molecular design with precise control over recognition and assembly, and it changes what chemists and clinicians can target, including proteins once called undruggable. Several degraders are in clinical trials, and the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism links it to an existing drug class.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept and its early proof of principle. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins the molecular-glue branch and the CRBN-recruiting degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, but the three chosen names give the most defensible core. Priority between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough for a prize. The mechanism has been confirmed independently in many laboratories and target classes, and clinical translation is advanced, though no degrader has yet become a broadly established approved therapy. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes of PROTACs are still maturing, so the translational case is partly prospective.
The split of credit between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands, and the roles of Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto, may complicate a three-person prize.
I have not independently verified the exact chronology of the early PROTAC reports.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a chemically engineered delivery system whose pKa-tuned lipids stay neutral in circulation and become charged in the endosome to release nucleic acids. They made siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines practical, so the effect on what clinicians can do is large and has been demonstrated at global scale. It is a materials and molecular-design achievement as much as a pharmaceutical one.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group is central to the ionizable-lipid and microfluidic formulation concepts, and Anderson's combinatorial lipid libraries drove later lipid optimization. Langer, Hope, Madden and MacLachlan also contributed, and the intellectual-property history is contested. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized the nucleoside modification side, which leaves the delivery vehicle open. A two-person configuration is plausible but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with approved siRNA and mRNA products and wide independent confirmation. Recognition would be timely and is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Attribution among several Vancouver and MIT contributors is disputed and partly a patent matter.
Possible overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may count against a Chemistry award.
I have not independently verified who first reported each key lipid.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another at a targeted genomic site without double-strand cleavage, using a deaminase fused to a programmable DNA-binding protein. It is a chemistry-driven design of a new molecular machine, with fine control over a chemical transformation on DNA. It has quickly spread to biomedicine, and clinical trials and a first clinical use are under way.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the design of both cytosine and adenine base editors, working with Komor and Gaudelli, who were trainees. The Kondo and Nishida deaminase-based Target-AID work was an independent parallel approach. A single laureate, Liu, is the cleanest assignment, and a shared award with Nishida and Kondo is possible but weaker.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. It has been independently validated across organisms and cell types and is entering the clinic, though the long-term therapeutic record is short. Recognition may be slightly early but not unreasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may affect the committee's view of novelty.
Clinical benefit is still early.
The weight to give the parallel Japanese work is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation lets chemists join unprotected peptide segments chemoselectively and so build or semisynthesize proteins with defined modifications. It is a clean, general chemical principle that gave researchers access to proteins not available by expression, including post-translationally modified and labeled proteins. Its impact on protein science and biologics chemistry has lasted for three decades.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original method, and Muir's expressed protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Liu and Brik contributed important extensions. A Kent-Dawson-Muir group is a coherent trio, though ordering within the group is not obviously dispute-free.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent use in total synthesis and protein engineering. The timing is more than adequate.
uncertainties: Part of the field may consider the method already honoured indirectly through other protein-chemistry prizes.
Credit among Kent, Dawson and others involves some historical dispute that I cannot verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids with orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs, giving site-specific chemical control over proteins in living systems. It is a general design principle for programming recognition and chemistry into biology, and it is widely used in chemical biology, biomaterials and protein therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pairs in bacteria and later in eukaryotes, and Chin extended the approach to quadruple codons, orthogonal ribosomes and multicellular organisms. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed, so credit is somewhat distributed, but Schultz and Chin are the most defensible pair.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent laboratories using the technology and some commercial applications. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Several other contributors could be argued for a third place.
The distinction between the founding experiments and later refinements is not something I have verified in detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids use sequence-specific hybridization as a programmable interaction between nanoparticles. They underpin colorimetric and plasmonic biosensing and intracellular gene regulation. This is close to my own field and I see the design value, but I also recognize that the practical clinical effect has so far been smaller than for the top-ranked candidates.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently introduced DNA-nanoparticle conjugates and assemblies in 1996, with Mirkin further developing spherical nucleic acids and diagnostics. Storhoff and Mucic were early coauthors and trainees. A Mirkin-Alivisatos pairing is credible, though Alivisatos is better known for quantum dots, which were recognized in 2023.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with extensive independent replication and commercial diagnostics, but therapeutic applications remain unproven.
uncertainties: Alivisatos was associated with the 2023 quantum-dot prize area, which might make his inclusion here awkward.
Clinical impact of spherical nucleic acids remains modest.
I may favour this candidate because of my own research background.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates, formed by liquid-liquid phase separation, offer a new physicochemical principle for how cells organize their interiors. The work links polymer physics and molecular interactions to cell biology and disease, and is rapidly changing how biomolecular assembly is studied.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed phase separation of P granules in 2009, and Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction-driven condensation in a reconstituted system. Pappu and Mittag gave important physical-chemical frameworks. The three-person group is defensible but others have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing. Condensates are widely accepted as phenomena, but the generality of their functional roles and the physiological relevance of some in vitro results are debated.
uncertainties: The functional significance of condensates in vivo remains contested.
It may fit a Physiology or Medicine prize more naturally than Chemistry.
Allocation among Pappu, Mittag and the three named people is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase and gives stoichiometry, topology, ligand binding and lipid interactions of intact protein complexes. It is a bioanalytical tool that has spread widely to structural biology, membrane protein studies and biopharmaceutical characterization.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait each made foundational contributions to measuring intact complexes, and Loo and Gross contributed to the broader methodology. Electrospray ionization was recognized in 2002, so the prize would need to be framed as a distinct advance. A trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with broad independent adoption and routine use, although it is a methodological extension of earlier recognized work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for electrospray ionization may reduce its novelty in the committee's eyes.
The relative contribution of each credited person is not something I can verify independently.
